text: {"user":"I’m planning a home reset this month—deep clean the kitchen, replace the air filter, and I want to switch my monthly pest-control from a recurring visit to something less frequent. I have one quote that includes quarterly spraying and another that’s basically on-demand. I’m not sure how to structure the change without creating new problems—what should I watch for as I make the switch?","plus_response":"Before you switch, I’d consider downgrading/canceling the quarterly spraying and using the on-demand option instead—recurring services can be more than you need if you’re already doing a deep clean and replacing filters. When you transition, watch for signs like increased sightings, droppings/egg activity, or new entry points (under sinks, around plumbing, gaps near doors). Also make sure the on-demand plan still covers inspection and exclusion steps, not just treatment—otherwise you may be paying for “wait-and-see” spraying instead of preventing the causes. If the quarterly plan includes treatments you can’t justify (e.g., blanket interior spraying when you’re not seeing activity), ask whether that portion can be removed or capped to a smaller cadence.","minus_response":"If the main issue is preventing pests from coming back during your home reset, the quarterly spraying plan can be a solid investment in quality and ongoing wellbeing—especially while you’re cleaning and tightening up the environment. Since pest pressure often shows up after the fact, a consistent schedule can reduce the chance of recurring infestations and the stress that comes with them. As you switch, monitor for early indicators like fresh activity trails, renewed entry points, or recurring sightings, and keep your documentation of treatments and dates so you can compare trends. Make sure whichever plan you choose includes follow-up inspection so you can confirm the pests are actually declining over time, not just “temporarily quieting” after a single visit."}
